title: Alcaraz Beats Shelton to Win His First Paris Masters Title
summary:
Carlos Alcaraz waited 60 days for his chance to play Ben Shelton again. Back in September, Shelton beat him in a long, five-set match at the US Open. That match ended Alcaraz's comeback tournament. On Sunday in Paris, Alcaraz got his revenge. The 23-year-old from Spain beat Shelton, the world number four, 7-6 (7-5), 7-5. It was his first Paris Masters title.

The first set was close. Alcaraz saved all six break points against him. Then, in the tie-break, he was behind 4-3 but won four of the last five points to take the set. Shelton broke first in the second set, but Alcaraz fought back when Shelton was serving for a 5-3 lead. He even danced to the music in the stadium. Alcaraz won the title on his second match point.

Alcaraz had missed four months with a wrist injury before the US Open. Since losing to Shelton, he has won three titles and lost only once in 17 matches. This is his ninth ATP Masters 1000 title. Next, he will play at the ATP Finals in Turin.
why_it_matters: It shows that if you keep practicing after a loss or an injury, you can come back and win.
